newsitem.title: HONG KONG: British forces in HK salute Queen...er, sorry Duke.
newsitem.headline: British forces in HK salute Queen...er, sorry Duke.

text.p: A British forces press advisory featured a 21-gun salute on Tuesday by the frigate HMS Chatham in Hong Kong harbour in honour of Queen Elizabeth's birthday.
Trouble is, Tuesday's the birthday of her husband, the Duke of Edinburgh.

"I don't know what bit of paper you're referring to but our press release dated June 6 clearly stated that the salute is in honour of the Duke of Edinburgh's birthday," said a slightly flustered spokeswoman for the British garrison in Hong Kong.

"Today is the Duke of Edinburgh's biological birthday and he is however old he is and we are saluting it. We fired a salute on February 6 to honour the Queen's accession and another on April 21 to honour her birthday and a third on June 2 to honour her coronation."

But an undated handout from the British military headquarters public relations staff lists upcoming events "involving the British garrison" as including: "June 10- 21-gun salute-HM The Queen's official birthday."

Ruffles and flourishes and 21-gun salutes in honour of the Royal family will come to an end in Hong Kong at midnight on June 30 when the territory is handed back to China after 156 years under British control.
Memo to press office: It was the Duke's 76th birthday.
